summary: Madagascar’s pledges mix restoration, conservation and agriculture. The central cross-sector commitment restores 1.6 million ha of terrestrial ecosystems—about 6.3% of its 2022 mapped forest—while the document also cites a 4 million-ha AFR100 ambition by 2030 and 1,907 kt CO₂ eq of additional sequestration in 2030 and 2035. Restoration ranges from 75,000 ha planted annually and 20,000 ha in hydropower basins to 170,000 ha of mangroves by 2030; a separate 500,000-ha ecosystem goal by 2030 equals about 2.0% of mapped forest. Conservation strengthens 428,134 ha of protected areas and protects 7,907 ha of seagrass by 2035, with 25,000 ha of avoided deforestation every five years. Agriculture and cross-sector measures cover 500,000 ha under sustainable practices and soil management by 2035, 350,000 ha of conservation agriculture by 2035, and 120,000 farms under agroforestry by 2035; the 500,000-ha farming area is about 6.1% of 2022 mapped agriculture.
